title: Mosloflavone from Fissistigma petelotii ameliorates oncogenic multidrug resistance by STAT3 signaling modulation and P-glycoprotein blockade.
authors: Chien, Po-Yu; Lan, Yu-Hsuan; Wu, I-Ting; Huang, Yu-Pin; Hung, Chin-Chuan
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物mosloflavone通过STAT3信号和P-gp阻断逆转肿瘤多药耐药，仅含分子对接模拟，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Oncogenic multidrug resistance (MDR) is a tough question in cancer therapy. However, no effective medications targeting oncogenic MDR are currently available. Studies have demonstrated that mosloflavone exerts anti-inflammatory effects, yet, its potential to ameliorate MDR remains unclear. PURPOSE: This study aimed to access the capability and elucidate molecular mechanisms of mosloflavone as a MDR resensitizing candidate. METHODS: We investigated the ability of mosloflavone to reverse oncogenic MDR and investigated its underlying mechanisms through cytotoxicity assay, cell cycle assay, apoptosis assay, and zebrafish xenograft model. The modulatory interplay between mosloflavone and P-gp was investigated through analysis of calcein-AM uptake, substrate efflux, ATPase assays, and molecular docking simulation. RESULTS: Mosloflavone inhibited P-gp efflux function in an uncompetitive manner without altering ABCB1 gene expression. In addition, it stimulated P-gp ATPase activity by binding to an active site distinct from that of verapamil. Regarding MDR reversal potential, mosloflavone resensitized MDR cancer cells to chemotherapies by arresting cell cycle and triggering apoptosis, possibly by enhancing reactive oxygen species accumulation and reducing phospho-STAT3. Moreover, in the zebrafish xenograft model, mosloflavone significantly potentiated the antitumor effect of paclitaxel. CONCLUSION: Our findings underscore the potential of mosloflavone as a novel dual modulator of STAT3 and P-gp, indicating it is a promising candidate for overcoming MDR in cancer treatment.
abstract_zh: 背景：致癌性多药耐药（MDR）是癌症治疗中的一个难题。然而，目前尚无有效针对致癌性MDR的药物。研究表明，mosloflavone具有抗炎作用，但其改善MDR的潜力尚不清楚。目的：本研究旨在评估mosloflavone作为MDR增敏候选药物的能力，并阐明其分子机制。方法：我们通过细胞毒性试验、细胞周期试验、凋亡试验和斑马鱼异种移植模型，研究了mosloflavone逆转致癌性MDR的能力及其潜在机制。通过calcein-AM摄取分析、底物外排、ATP酶试验和分子对接模拟，研究了mosloflavone与P-gp之间的调节性相互作用。结果：Mosloflavone以非竞争性方式抑制P-gp外排功能，且不改变ABCB1基因表达。此外，它通过与维拉帕米不同的活性位点结合，刺激P-gp ATP酶活性。在MDR逆转潜力方面，mosloflavone通过阻滞细胞周期和触发凋亡，使MDR癌细胞对化疗药物重新敏感，可能通过增强活性氧积累和减少磷酸化STAT3实现。此外，在斑马鱼异种移植模型中，mosloflavone显著增强了紫杉醇的抗肿瘤效果。结论：我们的研究结果强调了mosloflavone作为STAT3和P-gp新型双重调节剂的潜力，表明它是克服癌症治疗中MDR的有前景的候选药物。
